startup.name: Vorflux
startup.one_liner: A cloud-based AI coding agent for teams
startup.description: A cloud coding agent for teams that takes work from a ticket or message through planning, implementation, review, testing and a pull request. Parallel agents, different models for planning and adversarial review, codebase memory, dedicated compute per team with QA agents testing in a real browser and recording video, integrations with GitHub, Linear, Slack, Jira and others, bring your own model, and help setting up the harness. Team size unknown.

yc_acceptance.basis: Note only because the company is already accepted. A random applicant starts near 1 percent. A polished and technically specific product in the hottest category is above the base, but cloud coding agents are the most crowded area of YC applicants and the team size is unknown.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because the pitch looks like a well built version of what Cursor, OpenAI and Cognition already ship, with no stated traction or reason a lab would not copy it. Reviewers have seen a very large number of coding agent applications. Investors would also compare the company with the closest analogs in the data, most of which stalled at this step without clear revenue or a durable advantage over better funded rivals.

killers.risk: Model labs and Cursor ship the same cloud agent features
killers.evidence: Gartner's May 2026 quadrant names Anthropic, Cursor, GitHub and OpenAI as leaders in enterprise coding agents, and they bundle agents with the models.
killers.mitigation: Be the neutral harness across models and focus on QA with video evidence for teams that use multiple vendors.

killers.risk: Token costs and routing erode gross margins
killers.evidence: Running parallel agents with adversarial review multiplies model calls while prices vary by vendor.
killers.mitigation: Route to cheaper models and price by outcomes.

killers.risk: No traction beyond pilots in a crowded launch cycle
killers.evidence: Coding agent launches are frequent and teams switch easily. and this pattern is visible in the cited analogs.
killers.mitigation: Win a small number of teams with a hands on onboarding.

killers.risk: Enterprise security and compute demands for dedicated environments
killers.evidence: Dedicated compute per team is costly to operate for an early company. and this pattern is visible in the cited analogs.
killers.mitigation: Start with fewer customers and use managed cloud.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating parallel agents, browser based testing with video and codebase memory is mostly engineering on top of public models. A small team can build it in three months but also a rival can, so the complexity is not a moat. The dedicated compute per team adds operational work.

takeover_risk.rationale: The leaders already ship cloud agents with parallel execution and have the model access, distribution and capital to add QA video and integrations within months. This is the highest takeover risk category in the data.

evidence.claim: Gartner puts the enterprise AI coding agent market near $9.8B to $11B annualized in April 2026 and forecasts most engineers will use agents by 2028.
Coding agents reached about $2B ARR for the leading product, a sign of paid demand.

roadmap.goal: Ten teams in weekly use and a clear reason to pick this over bundled agents.
actions: Win ten engineering teams with hands on harness setup.
Publish results on merged pull requests per week and bug escape rate.
roadmap.proof: Ten paying teams and a measured gain in merged work.

roadmap.goal: Repeatable enterprise sales and net revenue retention.
actions: Add SSO, audit logging and compliance.
Prove gross margin with model routing.
roadmap.proof: Annual recurring revenue above $1M and gross margin above 60 percent.

pros.evidence: The description includes QA with video, model routing and onboarding help, which suggests a working product.

pros.point: Neutral across models is a real enterprise want
pros.evidence: Bring your own model is in the pitch and enterprises avoid vendor lock in.

brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Vorflux" --era 2022+ : kind invented_or_proper, alive 92.7 percent in cohort n=1826
weaknesses: Hard to spell and meaningless without context
brand.rationale: An invented word that is unique and available but gives no clue about the product. Invented names are the most common in YC and show average survival, and developer tools such as Greptile and Ellipsis show that distinctive names work for this audience.

narrative.headline: A well specified product in the most crowded, platform exposed category, with seed odds at the base rate and a lower tail from model lab competition.
narrative.general_summary: Vorflux is a cloud coding agent that takes tickets to pull requests with QA video evidence. The market is large and growing, with Gartner counting about $10B and the leaders growing fast. The same facts make it the hardest category to stand out in, because Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and GitHub ship similar features. A seed above the YC check is as likely as the AI cohort base rate. Later rounds depend on a clear wedge, as Greptile found in code review. About 50 percent of forecast paths end in a stall or shutdown.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2026-10-05 using only the batch listing; team size is not stated.
Greptile's Series B in October 2026 and later events were not used as evidence.
The step seed means a round above about $500K within roughly 12 months of the batch start.
